## My Thinking

My family has farmed this land in Quzhou my whole life. My father grew wheat and maize. I grow wheat and maize. That's what the land here does — the North China Plain is flat, the soil is decent, and the markets in town buy both reliably. I have about 10 mu, and I'll put all of it into the wheat-maize rotation like every year.

I plant winter wheat in October after the summer maize comes off. I harvest wheat in June, then turn around and get maize in the ground fast before the summer heat peaks. Two crops per year. That's how you make money on 10 mu.

For wheat, I use Kenong 199 — that's what most people in the village use, it's been solid for years. For maize I always buy Zhengdan 958 hybrid seed from the input shop in town. Hybrid maize gives you more, everyone switched years ago.

Fertilizer: I put down base fertilizer before planting and top-dress in spring for wheat. I know the extension station people say we use too much, but I've seen what happens when neighbors cut back — they regret it. I'd rather spend a bit more on fertilizer than lose yield. For irrigation, wheat needs water at winter, jointing, and heading — I do 4 waterings to be safe. Maize needs less, maybe 2 times unless it's a dry summer.

I rotary till before wheat planting to work in the maize stubble, and again before maize planting to break up the wheat stubble.
